entries.test: Public recordings and transcripts of Altman's AI discussions before publication would show whether he ever described a real-world use case.
entries.note: The mocking framing accompanies a concrete, categorical assertion about his public statements.
The explanation depends on Altman's private motives and what he wants people to know.

entries.test: Public financial disclosures and documented deployments available by publication would show whether companies other than Klarna had improved profits through generative AI.
entries.note: Read as a qualified claim about available evidence, rather than an unrestricted assertion that no such companies exist.

entries.test: Employment records, company disclosures, and documented outcomes of AI worker replacements available at publication would establish their scale and operational results.
entries.note: “Does not appear” qualifies the available evidence; the sentence still makes an empirical claim about displacement and results.
This is a counterfactual argument about what firms would already be doing if AI had the stipulated capabilities.

entries.test: Documented advances using technology already available at publication would show whether generative AI could substantially improve and overcome its identified limitations without the claimed breakthroughs.
entries.note: The extraction captures the asserted technical limitation within the claim about Altman's beliefs. “May never” qualifies future invention, not the firm assertion that missing technology is necessary.

entries.test: Sora's public launch date and contemporaneous court filings would show whether its launch immediately prompted a major legal fight over training data.
entries.note: Sora's public launch has occurred. The training-data inference is hedged, but the predicted legal consequence is firm.
The preceding sentence supplies the lawsuit-loss condition. “Possibly necessitating” makes the predicted retraining and licensing consequences a possibility.

entries.test: Following a broad decline in AI usage, public revenue reports and data-center utilization evidence would show whether big-tech revenue fell and substantial facilities sat unused.
entries.note: This sentence makes the outcomes conditional on declining usage, without specifying a deadline for that condition.
